snippet.title: Still Not Pregnant on Clomid? Check This First
snippet.description:
Taking Clomid (clomiphene) but still not pregnant? Dr Senai Aksoy, Associate Professor of Reproductive Medicine, starts with the question that decides what comes next: did the treatment actually trigger ovulation? Not ovulating and ovulating without getting pregnant are two different situations, and each needs a different next step.

In short: the French prescribing information sets a maximum of six treatment cycles, and three courses at the recommended dose without ovulation means the trial is over. Clomiphene has not been shown to improve egg quality, and used alone in women who already ovulate with unexplained infertility it has not shown benefit. For ovulation problems caused by PCOS, with no other fertility factor, the 2023 international guideline places letrozole first line. Warning signs matter too: vision changes mean stopping the treatment and contacting your doctor.

CHAPTERS
00:00 Still no pregnancy on Clomid?
00:20 Ovulating or not: two different stories
01:25 How clomiphene works
01:48 Does a bigger follicle mean a better egg?
02:11 Scenario 1: no ovulation (PCOS, thyroid, prolactin, weight)
02:41 Letrozole first line in PCOS: the 2023 guideline
03:10 Scenario 2: ovulation, but no pregnancy
03:46 Unexplained infertility: clomiphene alone
04:14 How many cycles are too many?
04:46 What comes next: injections, insemination, IVF
05:12 Monitoring: ultrasound and hormone tests
05:47 Safety: vision changes and emergencies
06:38 Three questions to ask your doctor

MORE ON OUR WEBSITE
• PMOS (formerly PCOS): diagnosis, treatment and fertility: https://www.draksoyivf.com/blog/polycystic-ovary-syndrome
• Unexplained infertility: what the diagnosis means and what usually comes next: https://www.draksoyivf.com/blog/demystifying-unexplained-infertility
• IVF for ovulation disorders (PCOS / PMOS): when to consider it: https://www.draksoyivf.com/blog/ivf-as-an-option-for-women-with-ovulation-disorders
• IUI with a partner's sperm: who it helps and what success rates mean: https://www.draksoyivf.com/blog/iui-with-partner-explained-success-rates-2025

SOURCES
• International PCOS guideline 2023 (ASRM summary): https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/recommendations-from-the-2023-international-evidence-based-guideline-for-the-assessment-and-management-of-polyendocrine-metabolic-ovarian-syndrome-2023
• Cochrane review: Letrozole versus clomiphene for ovulation induction (Franik 2022): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36165742/
• Cochrane review: Clomiphene for unexplained subfertility (Hughes 2010): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20091498/
• French prescribing information for clomiphene (ANSM, SmPC): https://base-donnees-publique.medicaments.gouv.fr/medicament/65338028/extrait

Already taking clomiphene? Do not stop, restart or change the dose on your own; review it with your doctor. If you have blurred vision, flashes of light, spots in front of your eyes, severe abdominal pain, rapid swelling of the belly or shortness of breath, contact your doctor straight away. In an emergency, call your local emergency number (911 in the US, 999 in the UK).

What would you like to ask about ovulation or fertility treatment? Leave a question in the comments without sharing private medical details. Subscribe to Dr. Aksoy — Fertility, No Hype for clear explanations to help you prepare for discussions with your own doctor.

For more information:
WhatsApp: +90 507 380 28 05
Website: https://www.draksoyivf.com

MEDICAL INFORMATION
This video is for education and information only. It is not personal medical advice, a diagnosis or a treatment recommendation. Your individual circumstances require assessment by a qualified clinician. Do not start, stop or change medication based on this video without consulting your doctor. Prescribing rules, including whether letrozole may be used for ovulation induction, differ between countries.

LANGUAGE AND PRODUCTION
This is an English-dubbed version of Dr Aksoy's original French educational video, using an AI voice based on Dr Aksoy's own voice. Lip movements were adjusted with AI to match the English audio. Humorous clips are illustrations (stock footage and an AI-generated cartoon) and are labeled on screen.
